channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-mac
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: unbraid — via awesome-mac
item.description: Per-app VPN client. Each app can use its own exit or skip the VPN, while Tailscale stays on.

item.title: Tietie — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source clipboard history for Mac and Windows with number-key pasting and search for text inside images, with an interface in Traditional Chinese.

item.title: TernaryCode — via awesome-mac
item.description: Terminal workspace for many projects and the coding agents in them that shows which agent is waiting for you.

item.title: SIAM.AI GPU Watch — via awesome-mac
item.description: Menu bar app for monitoring NVIDIA GPUs across remote servers over SSH.

item.title: Meridian — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source Arc-style browser on Chromium with spaces, pinned tabs, a command bar, one-click Arc and Chrome import, and a built-in MCP server for AI agents.

item.title: HyprMac — via awesome-mac
item.description: Keyboard-driven tiling window manager inspired by Hyprland, with automatic dwindle layout and ten workspaces.

item.title: Driftwall — via awesome-mac
item.description: Play any video file as a looping live wallpaper behind your desktop icons, on every display.

item.title: Deskbridge — via awesome-mac
item.description: Menu bar app that opens a Samsung Galaxy phone's DeX desktop in a Mac window over USB or Wi-Fi, with phone apps in their own windows, call banners and notifications.

item.title: mm2t — via awesome-mac
item.description: Meeting recorder with local storage and on-device speaker recognition, using your chosen services for transcripts and summaries.

item.title: Xylem — via awesome-mac
item.description: Native terminal for Claude Code with tabs that resume their sessions, context and cost tracking, and a panel for project skills, MCP and git.

item.title: WhimsyDesk — via awesome-mac
item.description: Real-feeling desktop objects (a fridge, a drawer, a post box, a vending machine) that hold your files and put them back where they were.

item.title: Pixtamer — via awesome-mac
item.description: Batch convert, compress, resize and rename images into web-ready JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF, with responsive widths and presets. Nothing is uploaded.

item.title: OmegaStar — via awesome-mac
item.description: Turns the Claude Code you already use, with its browser, models and logins, into a team of AI employees with scoped objectives, who learn by talking and keep each lesson as a skill.

item.title: Inquiline — via awesome-mac
item.description: Runs real Android 15 on Apple Silicon and turns each Android app into its own Mac app, with Gemini over any app, Android widgets on the desktop and per-app ad blocking.

item.title: DropKeeper — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source app that gives every new download an expiry and moves expired files to the Trash, with Undo.

item.title: Better Wacom — via awesome-mac
item.description: Per-app ExpressKeys, long-press actions and multi-mode dials for the Wacom Intuos Pro M (2025, PTK-670), running next to the official driver.

item.title: App Vanish — via awesome-mac
item.description: Drop an app on the bin to remove it and the files it left behind. Unsure files start unticked and everything goes to the Trash. The App Store edition finds leftovers of apps you already deleted.

item.title: YANA — via awesome-mac
item.description: Turns the MacBook notch into a Dynamic Island for media, volume and brightness HUDs, notifications, Messages, iPhone calls, calendar, weather, timers, and a file shelf.

item.title: Pinto Notes — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source notes app that ChatGPT, Claude and other AI assistants can search and edit over MCP, with each AI edit highlighted and undoable.

item.title: Papilot — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source desktop app where you annotate the compiled PDF, run coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor in isolated Git worktrees, and review rendered before-and-after PDF diffs before merging.

item.title: Inkstone (砚台) — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source Markdown workspace with a wiki built from selected notes and AI answers that cite original passages (source preview for Apple Silicon).

item.title: Hourmint — via awesome-mac
item.description: Menu bar time tracker for freelancers with a work log, timesheets and PDF invoices.

item.title: Fenestra — via awesome-mac
item.description: Windows 11 desktop for macOS with a taskbar, Start menu, Snap Layouts, Alt+Tab and clipboard history.

item.title: DisplayLatch — via awesome-mac
item.description: Keeps external monitors connected after sleep and restart, with DDC brightness, resolution and disconnect-without-unplugging controls.

item.title: Agent Monitor — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source desktop widgets and menu bar app that show which Claude Code and Codex sessions are waiting on you, open them on click, and track usage limits.

item.title: zest — via awesome-mac
item.description: Autocomplete popup for zsh with descriptions for 1,500 commands, in Terminal.app, iTerm2, Ghostty, VS Code and Cursor.

item.title: WhisPaste — via awesome-mac
item.description: Push-to-talk dictation for macOS, Windows and Linux that transcribes on-device with Whisper or Parakeet and pastes the text at the cursor in any app.

item.title: Velinshot — via awesome-mac
item.description: Free native screenshot editor with annotations, custom frames and local OCR (unnotarized preview).

item.title: Treewise — via awesome-mac
item.description: File manager that works like Windows Explorer: a folder tree, cut and paste, and two windows side by side.

item.title: Tomoru — via awesome-mac
item.description: Live bilingual subtitles for streams, anime, games, and meetings, plus instant screen text translation — works offline on your Mac or in the cloud, with glossaries that keep character names right.

item.title: Spool — via awesome-mac
item.description: Keyboard-driven email client written in Rust on gpui, the framework Zed is built with.

item.title: Seshka — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source menu bar app that finds the dev servers, watchers, and browsers closed Claude Code sessions left running, and kills them.

item.title: Point — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source push-to-talk dictation that also lets you circle part of the screen while you talk, sending your words plus a marked-up screenshot to Claude Code, Cursor, or any chat, transcribed on-device.

item.title: NotchDeck — via awesome-mac
item.description: Control center around the MacBook notch with system metrics, media controls, quick notes, screen recording and task profiles.

item.title: Music Router — via awesome-mac
item.description: Stops Music.app from auto-launching and routes media keys to the app you're actually using.

item.title: Linger — via awesome-mac
item.description: Local-first visual reference library for saving images, source links, and notes, with keyword search and collections.

item.title: Gesher — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source MCP servers and CLIs that let AI assistants read and edit Apple Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Maps, Weather and Freeform.

item.title: Escale — via awesome-mac
item.description: Native SSH client with tabs, an SFTP browser beside the terminal, tunnels, multi-execution and a built-in X11 server.

item.title: EdgeEver — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source note-taking and knowledge workspace with self-hosting, multi-device sync, and MCP integration.

item.title: ClaudeTTY — via awesome-mac
item.description: Native macOS terminal for running lots of Claude Code at once, where every tab keeps running after the app quits.

item.title: BitSpring — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source bit-perfect music player with native DSD, per-track sample rates up to 768 kHz and AutoEQ headphone EQ.

item.title: Bar27 — via awesome-mac
item.description: Menu bar manager for macOS 27 that hides icons per app and reveals them with a click, hover, or shortcut.

item.title: Aris — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source AI agent in the MacBook notch that you talk or type to, which acts in your apps with the AI you already use and asks before anything that sends, writes or deletes.

item.title: AGASTHY — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source app that maps your repos, runtimes, packages and AI coding agents into one knowledge graph, with token usage, impact analysis and safe disk cleanup.

item.title: SoloPDF — via awesome-mac
item.description: Local-first PDF reader and 20-tool offline document suite where highlights become plain Markdown notes, with on-device OCR, visual blink diff, and a 56-tool MCP server.

item.title: Scrollr — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source menu bar tool that reverses scroll direction for external mice only, so the trackpad keeps natural scrolling, with an on/off switch per mouse.

item.title: Purr — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source on-device dictation that types into any app with Parakeet or Whisper, plus meeting notes with speaker labels and summaries.

item.title: NotificationNanny — via awesome-mac
item.description: Moves and restyles notification banners and can replace the Notification Center panel with a customizable one.

item.title: Multron Download Manager — via awesome-mac
item.description: Multi-connection download manager with yt-dlp and BitTorrent support.

item.title: Memozia — via awesome-mac
item.description: Open-source meeting recorder with on-device transcription, speaker labels, summaries, and editable action items.
